definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese game of tossing and catching small fabric bags filled with beans or pellets, similar to juggling. Also refers to the beanbags themselves.

examples.japanese: おばあちゃんにお{手玉|てだま}を{教|おそ}わった。
examples.english: I learned otedama (beanbag juggling) from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: お{手玉|てだま}を5つ{使|つか}って{遊|あそ}ぶのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult to play with five beanbags.

examples.japanese: {手作|てづく}りのお{手玉|てだま}を{作|つく}った。

notes:
TRADITIONAL GAME:
・Traditionally played by girls
・Often accompanied by {童謡|どうよう} (children's songs)
・Passed down through generations

THE BAGS:
・Filled with {小豆|あずき} (azuki beans), {数珠玉|じゅずだま} (Job's tears seeds), or plastic pellets
・Made from colorful fabric, often in {俵型|たわらがた} (bale shape)
・Typically play with 3-5 bags

PLAYING STYLES:
・{振|ふ}り{玉|だま} (toss and catch from same hand)
・{寄|よ}せ{玉|だま} (gather scattered beanbags)
・Various patterns with counting songs

CULTURAL NOTE:
・One of the {昔|むかし}の{遊|あそ}び (traditional Japanese games)
・Often taught at {お正月|しょうがつ} (New Year) events
・Part of cultural preservation activities in schools

COLLOCATIONS:
・お{手玉|てだま}をする (to play otedama)
・お{手玉|てだま}で{遊|あそ}ぶ (to play with beanbags)
・お{手玉|てだま}を{投|な}げる (to toss beanbags)
